source.title: Episodic Memory Theory for the Mechanistic Interpretation of Recurrent Neural Networks
source.authors: Arjun Karuvally; Peter DelMastro; H. Siegelmann

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether independently initialized RNNs learn a common mechanism for a task, using spectral comparisons with a theoretical circuit rather than direct pairwise representation-similarity measures.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports the complex-argument MAE between the learned recurrent-weight spectrum and the spectrum predicted by the variable-binding circuit, across four tasks and configurations trained across 20 seeds. The accompanying test accuracies are noted with the rows but are not separate representation-convergence results. Figures showing example decompositions are not added as separate rows. The paper does not compare representations between pairs of models directly.
record.test_reason: Twenty seeds of same-architecture Elman RNNs are each compared with one theoretical circuit spectrum. Matching spectra imply a shared mechanism across initializations, up to a basis change. This is an indirect, non-pairwise test bearing on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also frame the convergence as evidence for the universality hypothesis. They note that high L2 or bottlenecks push RNNs toward nonlinear encodings.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares learned recurrent-weight eigenvalue arguments with a theoretically predicted circuit spectrum; it does not use a direct pairwise representation-similarity method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence varies with task, hidden size, and L2 regularization; the authors single out T1 with hidden size 64 and L2 0.0 as a bottleneck-superposition exception.
record.problems: The evidence comes from toy algorithmic tasks and single-layer Elman RNNs, and the spectral comparison is an indirect proxy rather than a direct pairwise comparison of learned features or subspaces. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates. Several Table 1 errors are indeterminate because of rank differences, and several conditions have chance-level test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: None of the Table 1 task/configuration results were left out. Example weight decompositions and hidden-state visualizations in Figures 3–8 were not entered as separate rows because they do not report separate numerical cross-model convergence measurements.

untested.parts: No direct pairwise comparison of features or subspaces between seeds. Results are averages over 20 seeds with no per-seed spread. Only single-layer Elman RNNs on toy linear binary tasks.
No scale or capability sweep. No differing architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal data.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests between models.
No cross-model test of recurring neurons, SAE features or circuits beyond the spectrum-to-theory comparison.
No comparison across similarity metrics or input distributions.
No test of plateau, or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

missing.what: Gaussian initialization yields spectra with matching arguments but larger eigenvalue magnitudes; this holds for most seeds but not every seed.
Repeat copy with 16×5 vectors learns a nonlinear encoding with 63 rather than 80 near-unit eigenvectors, deviating from the linear circuit.
In some cases the basis transformation fails to reveal the interpretable circuit even when the spectrum converges.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is indirect: each seed's eigenvalue arguments are compared with a theoretical operator, ignoring magnitudes, and no uncertainty is reported. Rows at L2 0.1 have chance accuracy, so they are uninformative; cannot_determine is correct. The authors cite Li et al. 2015 (an original source) but are not themselves an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep testing whether alignment rises with model size or capability; no models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption inputs or vision-language models.

The study compares each trained RNN's spectrum with a theoretical circuit, rather than directly comparing learned features or subspaces between pairs of independently initialized networks. It does not test other architectures or tasks beyond the reported algorithmic RNN tasks.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No systematic cross-model test of recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
No comparison of similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions.
The paper reports a bottleneck-superposition exception, but does not test whether incomplete alignment is caused by shared training data or objectives, or whether alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: Elman RNNs (20 seeds; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the complex arguments of the learned Whh eigenspectrum with the theoretical Φ eigenspectrum; MAE is indeterminate because the ranks differ.
rows.measure: MAE in complex argument between predicted Φ spectrum and learned Whh spectrum
rows.locator: Table 1; Results, “RNNs consistently converge to the variable binding model”
rows.note: The authors explicitly identify this as an exception: despite high generalization accuracy, the network does not converge to the theoretical mechanism, attributed to bottleneck superposition and a low-rank representation.
rows.check: The value is indeterminate (rank mismatch). The authors say this configuration does not converge to the circuit despite 0.97 accuracy. Non-convergence to the theorized circuit does not by itself show that seeds diverge from each other. Keep as partial, with this caveat.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V3. MAE is indeterminate because theoretical and empirical ranks differ; average test accuracy is 0.97. Departure from the theoretical circuit does not establish incomplete convergence across seeds.
source_check.locator_found: Table 1 and caption; Section 7, first results subsection.
source_check.problem: The bottleneck limits the theoretical circuit model, but the reported measurement cannot determine convergence across seeds in this condition.

relationships.condition: Configurations with determinate MAE and high test accuracy (hidden 128, or tasks T2–T4 at hidden 64 with sufficient dimensions)
relationships.reason: Mean complex-argument MAE of 0.0005–0.0112 across 20 seeds indicates convergence to the same circuit spectrum (r04, r07, r10, r11, r13, r14, r16, r17, r19, r20, r22, r23).
relationships.display_finding: Mean complex-argument MAE ranged from 0.0005 to 0.0112 across 20 seeds, indicating closely aligned circuit spectra.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Configurations with determinate MAE and high test accuracy (hidden 128, or tasks T2–T4 at hidden 64 with sufficient dimensions)
source_check.reason: The listed rows report mean spectral-argument errors of 0.0005–0.0112 across 20 seeds relative to the theoretical circuit. This supports recurring circuit structure indirectly, without directly measuring pairwise feature or subspace alignment.

relationships.condition: Dimension bottleneck (T1, hidden 64, L2 0); per the text also nonlinear encodings and Gaussian initialization
relationships.reason: In r01, a high-accuracy network does not reach the circuit because of bottleneck superposition. The text (Fig. 6, App. B.4) adds nonlinear low-rank solutions and seed-dependent spectra.
relationships.display_finding: A high-accuracy network failed to recover the theoretical linear circuit because of bottleneck superposition; additional analyses found nonlinear low-rank solutions and seed-dependent spectra.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Dimension bottleneck (T1, hidden 64, L2 0); per the text also nonlinear encodings and Gaussian initialization
source_check.reason: r01 has indeterminate spectral MAE and establishes failure of the theoretical linear circuit, not failure of convergence across seeds. Figure 6 likewise concerns nonlinear compression. Appendix B.4 reports initialization-dependent eigenvalue magnitudes while Figure 8 retains aligned spectral arguments; these observations do not establish a V3 limitation.

relation.reason: The study reports its own evidence of recurring learned circuit structure across initializations, bearing on V3.

tranche.reason: Comparing learned spectral arguments across 20 seeds with a shared theoretical circuit provides an indirect test of V3 using a different method from direct representation-similarity comparisons.

source_check.notes: Spectral-argument agreement is indirect evidence of a shared mechanism, not a direct pairwise representation comparison or proof of identical features. Section 7 also reports that matching spectra can coexist with unsuccessful recovery of interpretable representations because basis construction is sensitive to numerical errors.

statements.correction: Table 1: T1; hidden size 64; L2=0; 20 seeds; average test accuracy 0.97; spectral MAE indeterminate because ranks differ. Section 7: bottleneck superposition produces a solution outside the theoretical circuit. Cross-seed feature or subspace divergence in this condition is not established.
statements.problem: The bottleneck condition, 0.97 accuracy, and departure from the predicted circuit are correct. Their use as a V3 limits_scope result is unsupported: departure from one theoretical circuit does not show that independently initialized networks fail to share features or subspaces.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported configurations with numeric low spectral errors and strong task accuracy
reader_labels.reason: The learned spectra are close to the predicted circuit spectra in these conditions, which the authors interpret as convergence to a common mechanism; see r04, r07, r10, r11, r13, r14, r16, r17, r19, r20, r22, r23.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that this high-accuracy setting does not converge to the proposed circuit, attributing the exception to bottleneck superposition; see r01.
